releases.summary:
The release v0.3.1 was going to be, plus everything the four days
spent chasing its release blocker turned up.

**Numbered 0.4.0 rather than 0.3.1 because the connector set
changed.** `rest` is new, so `profile.full.connectors` in BUILDINFO
is not what v0.3.0's was, and a package declaring
`requires.connectors` is checked against that list by name. A patch
digit over a changed compatibility surface is the one thing
BUILDINFO exists to prevent. `netcheck` is a new verb on the same
argument.

The headline for anyone deploying: **STUN ships for the first
time.** `drt stun`, the `stun` config block, and counters to the
supervisor all landed after v0.3.0 was tagged and have been sitting
unreleased since. So has the C host's `access` spelling, which is a
compatibility fix rather than a feature -- an existing discofetch
config does not parse on v0.3.0.
releases.upgrading:
**If you run configs written for the C host, this release is the one
that parses them.** v0.3.0 refused `access: "read"` and accepted
`"readonly"`, which is backwards; v0.4.0 matches `dhost.c` exactly.
A config that was edited to say `"readonly"` as a workaround must be
changed back -- `"readonly"` is now refused, by name, as it is by the
C host.

Nothing else in this release removes or renames a surface. `rest` and
`netcheck` are additive and reach nothing unless a config wires them:
`rest` answers no call at all without a scope granting origins, and
an empty allowlist is a startup refusal rather than a runtime
surprise.

added:
**STUN.** `drt stun` serves RFC 5389 binding requests, a `stun`
config block configures it, and inside `drt start` the same server
reports its counters to the root program. Two servers on separate
addresses is what makes mapping classification available at all:
one vantage says what one vantage saw, and it takes two to know
whether the mapping *changed*, which is the fact that decides
whether hole punching can work.

**`drt netcheck`.** One of four verdicts -- `direct`, `v6-direct`,
`punchable`, `relay` -- with the measurements that produced it, per
discofetch's `doc/NETCHECK-SPEC.md`. The verdict tree is a table
rather than nested branches, on that spec's own reasoning: it is
the part that will be wrong first when real home networks surprise
us, and a table is edited and re-tested.

The decisive measurement is the UDP mapping across two STUN
servers, never the TCP one. A NAT can be endpoint-independent for
TCP and symmetric for UDP, and reading the verdict off the TCP
columns would be confidently wrong on exactly the networks where
this matters most.

Reflect and the prober -- the edges' half -- are not implemented
here; the inbound test reports "not measured" until they exist.

**The `rest` connector: `host:rest/get` and `host:rest/post`.**
The guest surface is diluvium's, from
`plugins/rest/rest.plugin.json`, so a program written against
`diluvium-host` runs unchanged -- same calls, same shapes, and the
same bounds read out of `rest_plugin.c` rather than picked.
Redirects are not followed, because the C plugin does not follow
them.

Unlike the C host's out-of-process plugin, this takes a **scope**:
an origin allowlist, checked against the URL *and* against the
resolved address before connecting, since an allowed name that
resolves into private space is the DNS rebinding shape. An allow
entry may also carry `headers`, which the connector injects and the
guest can neither set nor read -- so a deployment calls an
authenticated API without the program ever holding the credential
-- and `allow_headers`, which when present is the exhaustive set
the guest may set on that origin.
`install.sh` ships as a release asset, so the one-liner has a URL that exists without waiting on server-side work.

`doc/HostBaseline.md`: the standard set of families any DRT host must provide or stub, measured against both hosts rather than reasoned about. Three mandatory (`time`, `time/monotonic`, `crypto/random`) and four rules, of which rule 3 has the teeth: a stub refuses, it never fakes.
`doc/FM-2-Upstream.md`: the brief for fixing FM-2 in diluvium.
This changelog, and `script/changelog.py` to generate and check it. Ported from diluvium's, shape and CLI intact.
changed:
**`access` is `read`, not `readonly`** -- a compatibility fix, and
the reason this is not optional for anyone running the C host's
configs. `dhost.c` accepts exactly `"read"` or `"readwrite"`; DRT
accepted `"readonly"` and *refused* `"read"`, so an existing
discofetch config fails DRT's parse and crash-loops under the
deploy chain check. Matched to the C host exactly, refusal wording
included, with a test in each connector pinning it.

`BUILDINFO.txt` now says what a binary carries: `dv_abi` (promised since v0.1.0 and never kept) and the connector set per profile, both read out of the artifact by `drt buildinfo` rather than guessed in YAML.

The README leads with a download that works today. The documented mirror URL 404s -- the mirror never grew the `drt` namespace -- and a doc that promises a 404 is how that went unnoticed. The mirror is still named as the intended front door, and named as not carrying the namespace yet.

`install.sh` verifies both sources. It carried a comment saying the GitHub fallback had no sums, true when written and false since the publish job started uploading `SHA256SUMS.txt`. A mismatch refuses; a missing sums file warns, so pinning an older release still works.
`DRT_MIRROR` takes `file://` URLs, which turns out to be the air-gapped install with no new code: point it at a directory and nothing touches the network.

`examples/hello.dlua` is rewritten against `host.*`, printing byte-identical output to the fifteen-line queue-boilerplate version it replaces. The old one is kept as `examples/by-hand.dlua`, as the honest illustration of what every `host.*` call does underneath.
fixed:
**FM-1: a use-after-free in tokio runtime teardown.** `drt relay`,
`drt stun` and `drt tunnel` dropped a `Runtime` on the way out,
which races a parked blocking worker's wakeup into a freed
`Condvar` in tokio 1.53.1. They leak it now. The exposure was a
clean shutdown turning into a SIGSEGV, which a supervised service
reads as a crash rather than a stop.

**FM-2: a data race in diluvium's continuation registries.**
`diluvium_shim_addcont` appends to a process-global array with no
synchronisation, so two threads calling `dv_new` at once can leave
a slot whose name is NULL and the next scan segfaults in `strcmp`.
DRT now serialises instance *creation* behind a mutex, which closes
it here; instances still run concurrently, one per thread.

The real fix is upstream and is not in this release. DRT's shipped
exposure was nil either way -- `run`, `start` and `repl` create
instances only on the drive-loop thread -- so this was a
test-harness crash for us and a live one for any host that creates
instances on more than one thread. See `doc/FM-2-Upstream.md`.

**A relay-only deployment burned a whole core.** With no HTTP listener the drive loop's idle sleep became a spin -- 99.7% CPU, forever, on exactly the rendezvous config `examples/rendezvous` documents. 3.0% now, which is the 1 ms tick doing its job.
The shipped `examples/deployment.json` did not load: the `access` fix above missed the one config file a new user copies. Found by running it rather than reading it.

`release.yml`'s publish job copied `install.sh` from one directory above the workspace, which does not exist. Under `set -eu` that failed the step and took the whole publish with it -- no release rather than a release missing an asset. Never caught because `publish` is the one job a rehearsal does not execute.
Linux non-x86_64 now refuses by name in `install.sh` instead of downloading the x86_64 static binary and failing the `--version` guard with "does not run here", which is true and no help at all.
`doc/Browser.md`'s export table listed fifteen functions and omitted `release`, which is a leak by construction for anyone implementing from it.
known_issues:
**FM-2 is open upstream.** The mutex above closes it for DRT. Any
other host embedding this diluvium revision and creating instances
from more than one thread still has the race.
**wasm32 is not in the release matrix, and the browser tier is
unwired.** `drt-web` compiles for wasm32 on every push but exports
only `memory`: there is no `wasm-bindgen` layer, no glue binding a
JS object to `HostBridge`, and no connector pump. Publishing an
artifact nothing can call would be a compatibility surface with
nothing behind it. See `doc/Next.md` for what it would take.
**`drt ps` is a stub.** The introspection surface it names is
designed and the data is all reachable in-process; what is missing
is the control endpoint it would reach a running deployment over,
which lands with sshd.
**The REPL has no line editor.** Pressing Up feeds a raw `\\x1b`
into the line, and since 0x1b is Lua's bytecode signature byte the
REPL answers "attempt to load a binary chunk". Architecturally
sound and unfinished; do not put a newcomer in front of it.
**Budgets bound the VM, not the deployment.** `instructions` and
`memory_kb` are properties of the guest VM. Neither bounds wall
time -- a hostcall that parks for 85 seconds consumes no
instructions -- nor cumulative spawns in a lineage. `doc/Next.md`
sizes both.

releases.summary:
The rendezvous relay, end to end: a real `ssh` session over WSS
through `drt tunnel`, 37 bytes metered, rehearsed against the release
artifact.

added: `drt relay`: the rendezvous relay -- parked WSS legs paired by label and spliced, with presence, metering and arbitration reported to the root program.
`drt tunnel`: SSH over WSS as a dumb pipe, in three shapes -- the OpenSSH `ProxyCommand` contract over stdio, a WS→TCP listener, and the device side of the relay.
known_issues: `access` is spelled `readonly` here and refuses `read`, which is backwards from the C host. A config written for `dhost.c` does not parse. Fixed in 0.4.0.
A relay-only deployment (no HTTP listener) spins a core at 99.7% forever. Fixed in 0.4.0.
`drt relay`, `drt stun` and `drt tunnel` can SIGSEGV on clean shutdown (FM-1). Fixed in 0.4.0.

releases.notes_md:
## [0.3.0] - 2026-08-28

`v0.3.0` · dv ABI 1 · diluvium `f137b308c4dc`

The rendezvous relay, end to end: a real `ssh` session over WSS
through `drt tunnel`, 37 bytes metered, rehearsed against the release
artifact.

### Connectors

- `full`: `time`, `fs`, `crypto`, `sql`, `ssh`, `listen`
- `slim`: `time`, `fs`, `crypto`, `listen`

### Added

- `drt relay`: the rendezvous relay -- parked WSS legs paired by label and spliced, with presence, metering and arbitration reported to the root program.
- `drt tunnel`: SSH over WSS as a dumb pipe, in three shapes -- the OpenSSH `ProxyCommand` contract over stdio, a WS→TCP listener, and the device side of the relay.

### Known issues

- `access` is spelled `readonly` here and refuses `read`, which is backwards from the C host. A config written for `dhost.c` does not parse. Fixed in 0.4.0.
- A relay-only deployment (no HTTP listener) spins a core at 99.7% forever. Fixed in 0.4.0.
- `drt relay`, `drt stun` and `drt tunnel` can SIGSEGV on clean shutdown (FM-1). Fixed in 0.4.0.
